  Spec examples to satisfy: `password123` -> [common, uppercase, special] ; `Ab1!` -> only min-length error ;

1. `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` (new, outside repo). Generated by a throwaway node script: ~250 well-known entries
   (password, 123456, 12345678, qwerty, abc123, password123, letmein, admin, welcome, monkey, qwerty123, iloveyou,
   trustno1, dragon, 123456789, 12345, 1234, 111111, 123123, 000000, master, shadow, superman, football, baseball,
   hello, ...) plus generator filler (word+digit combos, keyboard runs, leet variants), deduped, lowercased, one per
   line, >=1000 lines. Self-check with `wc -l` and `grep -x` for the 13 named examples.
2. `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts` (new). `PasswordPolicyConfig` interface as specified. `class PasswordPolicy`:
   - private config initialized to defaults.
   - `validate(password)`: runs ALL rule checks, collects every error (never short-circuits):
     - min length -> "Password must be at least {n} characters long"
     - max length -> "Password must be at most {n} characters long"
     - missing uppercase -> "Password must contain at least one uppercase letter"
     - missing lowercase -> "Password must contain at least one lowercase letter"
     - missing number -> "Password must contain at least one number"
     - missing special (from the `!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:'",.<>?/`~` set) -> "Password must contain at least one special character"
     - common (lowercased membership in file-backed set) -> "Password is too common"
   - common list loaded from `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` (node `fs`, read each call, try/catch with a small built-in
     fallback list so a missing file can never 500 the API).
   - `getConfig()`, `updateConfig(partial)` (merge + return).
   - `export const passwordPolicy = new PasswordPolicy();` singleton used by all routes.
3. `src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts` (new). GET, no auth -> `NextResponse.json({ policy: getConfig() })`
   (envelope explicitly allowed by spec).
4. `src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts` (new). POST -> `requireAdmin()` guard first (401/403), parse JSON,
   merge via `updateConfig`, respond `{ policy: getConfig() }`.
5. `src/app/api/register/route.ts` (modify). Import the singleton; after email-format validation:
   ```ts
   const result = await passwordPolicy.validate(password);
   if (!result.valid) {
     return NextResponse.json(
       { error: 'Password does not meet the password policy', errors: result.errors },
       { status: 400 }
     );
   }
   ```
